why: DECISION (manager 2026-11-19 10:41Z, data-backed Tier 2 under the standing rule): live-review-wake gets a VM-side clock via keeper_dispatch.sh, every 15 min (not 5), skipping when a run is already queued or in progress. Evidence: GitHub ran live-review-wake's */5 cron 4 times in 24 h (Actions API event=schedule, to 10:38Z; HOURLY-CRON-SCHEDULE-DROP, LTR-GH-WAKE-CRON-THROTTLED), and the repo queue was ~463 deep, so a 5-min dispatch would add ~288 runs/day to it. Change: deploy/trainer/ict-ltr-wake-dispatch.{service,timer} (OnCalendar :02/:17/:32/:47 UTC, same /etc/ict/gh-dispatch.env token and script as ict-keeper-dispatch, own latch); scripts/ops/keeper_dispatch.sh gains opt-in KEEPER_DISPATCH_SKIP_IF_ACTIVE=1 (reads queued + in_progress run counts first; an unreadable count is logged and the dispatch goes ahead); the installer enables both timers. Default behaviour of the hourly keeper floor is unchanged (test_default_never_reads_active_runs). Trainer VM only; no order path, no DB, no trader restart. Revert: sudo systemctl disable --now ict-ltr-wake-dispatch.timer. tests/test_keeper_dispatch.py 9 passed (4 new); backstop tests 25 passed. After merge: install via the trainer path and verify the first two timer fires each produce exactly one dispatch (or a logged skip). Gates this adds or changes: none.
